definition: Old MC CoG20+old energy window fixed; data same CoG20+window and LG tail veto. CT corrected MC pilot two files, original 1000 truth entries/file.

Observed integrated mean_temperature_C is arithmetic mean of retained hit temperatures/event, not calibrated reference temperature or measured event sensor average. Borrowed independently of MC truth; all hit signals use same event temperature, fully coherent scenario; no individual layer temperatures available. Within-run version removes observed run mean differences but retains global mean.

Fixed bias; Vov(T)=U20-0.06*(T-20), U20=4.5/4.0 V for 10/15um, pCT(T)=p20*(Vov/U20)^2 with p20=0.10/0.15. CT mean multiplicity 1/(1-p), approximate dilute branching. Gain ratio=1-alpha*(T-20), alpha=1.6/135 and3.5/230; PDE constant or linear Vov bracket. These curves are assumptions, not detector fits.

Raw model changes signal; gain_corrected divides by gain(T), leaving CT/PDE; full_response_corrected divides by whole modeled response and exactly cancels mean thermal variation. existing_correction_direction multiplies again by decreasing gain(T); diagnosis only, not recommended.

Independent product-distribution moment convolution of MC energy10/energy15 and empirical event-temperature distribution; fixed detected hit list, no reselection. Mean and RMS exact for this model, not a digitizer simulation.

Summary separates evaluating all events at empirical mean temperature from temperature distribution convolution; nonzero fixed-mean width shifts reflect differing10/15um energy reweighting, not random thermal broadening.

Gaussian/core are 24 reproducible random independent temperature assignments to original pilot events; mean and q16/q84 reflect assignment variation, not fit/systematic uncertainty. Gaussian two-pass240bin fit same as integrated diagnostics.

250 paired MC and data100-original-entry blocks, stratified sourcefile, exact modeled moments recomputed. Thermal distribution also block-resampled. q16/q84 are bootstrap sampling uncertainty, not model uncertainty.

No threshold changes, gain switching, saturation, pixel recovery, photon/CT fluctuations, within-layer temperature variation, or event-position/temperature covariance simulated. Common-temperature coherence is an envelope, not a demonstrated actual sensor covariance.

Converting a gain measured at24C to20C multiplies by1/(1-alpha*4), but a constant rescaling alone does not change relative resolution. Primary lightyield must not be recalculated at each temperature from MIP/gain(T).
Linearized temperature RMS needed to bridge data-minus-CTMC relative variance gap, using effective slope at empirical mean temperature; diagnostic of scale, not a fitted temperature fluctuation.
